Website says 3 left. Stockroom says sold out on Tuesday. Customer says "where's my order?"

If you build automations for shops, stock sync between the till and the website is boring, and worth every penny to the owner. Has this happened to a shop you work with?
ig:
Every clothing and shoe shop that sells in-store and online knows this one.

The till sells the last pair. The website doesn't hear about it until someone updates a spreadsheet. A customer pays for shoes that don't exist.

The fix isn't clever: when stock changes in one place, update the other, and alert someone when a count goes below a threshold. It's one of the most useful flows you can sell to a retailer.

What's the most boring automation that's paid you the best?
